result.instructions: Tools for WisePops, hosted by usefulapi.io. If the user is new or asks what this server can do, suggest requests such as: "Which of my WisePops pop-ups got the most email sign-ups?"; "Show the contacts my pop-ups collected since 1 November 2026."; "How many times was each pop-up displayed and clicked?". Read-only tools never change data; ask the user before a tool that creates, changes or deletes WisePops data. Free plan: 50 tool calls per month. Run wisepops_usage_status to see the calls used this month. If the user asks for something none of these tools can do, tell the user and, with their OK, run wisepops_request_feature to record the request. Paid plans: Pro (10,000 tool calls a month, $9/month or $90/year, for normal use) and Pro+ (100,000 tool calls a month, $39/month or $390/year, for automations and heavy use). A plan can be cancelled at any time and then runs to the end of the paid period, so it also suits a one-time job. When the user wants more calls or reaches the limit, run wisepops_upgrade without a plan: it returns both plans, each with a payment link for the user to open. wisepops_cancel_subscription cancels Pro at the end of the paid period.

tools.name: wisepops_list_popups
tools.title: List pop-ups
tools.description: List your WisePops pop-ups with their ID, label, activation state, creation date, and display, click and email counts. Use an ID as wisepop_id in wisepops_list_contacts. WisePops API: GET /api2/wisepops.

tools.name: wisepops_list_contacts
tools.title: List collected contacts
tools.description: List contacts (emails and other form fields) that your pop-ups collected, with the collection time, pop-up ID, IP and country. Filter by collected_after (UTC) and wisepop_id. Needs a WisePops Custom plan; standard usage is 1,500 API calls per 30 days. WisePops API: GET /api2/contacts.

collected_after.description: Only contacts collected after this UTC time, e.g. 2026-11-01T00:00:00Z.

wisepop_id.description: Only contacts from this pop-up ID (from wisepops_list_popups).
